Analytics that count reuse, not attention

Screens 8–13. Every figure here answers "was my work useful to someone" rather than "how many people looked". Readers are aggregated to institution and country before storage, and the team breakdown carries the same caution as the institutional dashboard — with the same teeth behind it.

THE PRIVACY DECISION, ON THE SCREEN
We do not record who reads your work. Reader identity is discarded at the edge and never written to storage — what is kept is an institution and a country, and only where at least three distinct readers from that institution have accessed the item in the period.
Why: a researcher who knows their browsing is logged reads less, and reads more defensively. The chilling effect costs more than the analytics are worth.
Consequence: you can never learn that a specific rival read your dataset. That is the trade, stated plainly, and it is not configurable.

Institutions under 3 readers—
The last row is the k-anonymity threshold working. An institution with two readers is two people, and naming it would identify them to anyone who knows the field.
READERS CAN OPT OUT ENTIRELY
A setting in your own account removes you from every institutional count, everywhere. Browsing without being counted is the default for logged-out visitors and one toggle for everyone else.
